turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first; who decided that, and on what basis?
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
You didn't answer me. Who decided, and was Owen heard before that zero went in? Then you can show me whatever you've got.
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided, and was Owen heard first?
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
I haven't said a word about any timestamp, and flattery won't change my position. You brought it up, so what timestamp, and what does it show?
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.

"Had to." Nobody has to enter a zero before calling a parent, and your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish anything. If there's a document with a date on it, put it in front of me; otherwise I'm going to the principal when we're done.
